title: Blockchain Week – UNGA Edition Announces Latest Round of Speakers and Expanded Leadership Team

Key appointments to the organizing team include:David Fung – Global Head of Institutional and Partnerships Jimmy Nguyen – Global Growth Officer Enyo Sam – Engineering & Marketing Lead The full roster features experts in institutional finance, cloud architecture, cybersecurity, real-world asset tokenization, Bitcoin mining, stablecoin infrastructure, and blockchain governance.Tickets and the complete speaker list are available at BlockchainWeek.ai.
contentHtml:
BLOCKCHAIN WEEK – UNGA EDITION

September 10–19, 2026 · Times Square, New York City

Flagship Conference at Hard Rock Times Square

NEW YORK, NY – August 18, 2026

Industry leaders from Amazon, AWS, Bakkt, Brevan Howard Digital, Crypto ISAC, Streamex, Liberland and leading global institutions confirmed for the premier blockchain gathering during United Nations General Assembly week. David Fung named Global Head of Institutional and Partnerships; Jimmy Nguyen appointed Global Growth Officer; Enyo Sam joins as Engineering & Marketing Lead.

Blockchain Week – UNGA Edition today announced the full latest round of approved speaker nominations together with three key leadership appointments to its organizing team. Speakers will appear at the Hard Rock Times Square flagship conference and across more than 100 events during the 10-day program running September 10–19, 2026, timed with the 81st United Nations General Assembly and New York Fashion Week.

Leadership Appointments

  • David Fung, Head of Institutional at Streamex Corp., has been appointed Global Head of Institutional and Partnerships. Streamex is a Nasdaq-listed real-world asset tokenization platform focused on bringing gold and other commodities on-chain. Fung will also speak at the conference.
  • Jimmy Nguyen, Founder & CEO of New Win Ventures and already announced speaker, has been appointed Global Growth Officer. A globally recognized blockchain leader and former Founding President of the BSV Blockchain Association, Nguyen specializes in intellectual property, data infrastructure and RWA tokenization.
  • Enyo Sam has been appointed Engineering & Marketing Lead. An AI-native developer, entrepreneur and founder of Easner (stablecoin banking infrastructure), Sam brings deep experience in fintech product development, cross-border payments, and marketing of emerging technology platforms. He is also a confirmed speaker and performer at the official after-party.

Featured Experienced Speakers

  • Kedar Mohile (Amazon) – 22+ years in cognitive security, GenAI architecture and privacy-first blockchain-enabled healthcare platforms.
  • Anisha Salunkhe (Amazon Web Services) – Cloud Applications Architect designing enterprise-scale systems processing millions of workflows daily.
  • Phillip Lord – CEO, Bitcoin Japan Corporation (TSE: 8105); former President of International at Bakkt; previously Jefferies, Nomura and HSBC.
  • Lewis Tuff – CTO, Brevan Howard Digital; formerly CTO of Blockchain.com; alumnus of Revolut, Goldman Sachs and UBS.
  • Justine Bone – Executive Director, Crypto ISAC; cybersecurity leader with experience at Bloomberg, Dow Jones and the intelligence community.
  • Eric Guthrie (eguthrie@cogentlaw.com) – Partner, Cogent Law; Director of Training, Government Blockchain Association; author of Blockchain or Die.
  • Wook Lee – CEO & Founder, EDENA Capital Partners; pioneer in sovereign-asset tokenization and climate-linked digital finance.
  • Ali Abou Daya – CEO, Transactix; blockchain and payments infrastructure expert since 2011; testified before Canadian Parliament.
  • Wassim Jarkas – Managing Director, iBLOCKCHAIN; thought leader in RWA tokenization and AI-driven digital transformation.
  • Cat Bonar – CEO, Block Reign; compliance and regulatory specialist for Web3 and real-world blockchain solutions.
  • Harshitha Ram – International arbitrator and mediator specializing in blockchain, crypto, AI and smart contracts; JAMS Fellow.
  • David Fung – Head of Institutional, Streamex Corp. (also Global Head of Institutional and Partnerships).
  • Dorian Jakov Štern Vukotić – Congressman & Blockchain Developer, Free Republic of Liberland.
  • Jimmy Nguyen – Founder & CEO, New Win Ventures (also Global Growth Officer).
  • Chris Ransdell – Bitcoin mining and energy specialist; advocate for efficient, renewable-aligned proof-of-work operations.
  • Enyo Sam – Founder of Easner stablecoin banking infrastructure (also Engineering & Marketing Lead).

Additional Confirmed Speakers

  • Srinivasa Rao Gunda
  • Suryasivaji Killi
  • Nithya Ramachandran
  • Akshay Pramod Roy
  • Samir Sengupta
  • Melody Fogarty
  • Li Maor

These speakers will contribute to high-signal programming covering Bitcoin and institutional infrastructure, tokenization of real-world assets, AI × Blockchain convergence, regulatory outlooks during UNGA season, energy transition, payments innovation, cybersecurity, and the emerging space economy.

“This complete roster of speakers and the appointments of David Fung, Jimmy Nguyen and Enyo Sam significantly strengthen both our content and our operational capacity,” said the organizers. “From Amazon and AWS cloud architecture to institutional RWA platforms, cybersecurity leadership, stablecoin infrastructure and global growth expertise, Blockchain Week – UNGA Edition now reflects the full maturity of the industry at a pivotal moment during the United Nations General Assembly.”

The centerpiece remains the two-day flagship conference at Hard Rock Times Square (September 16–17), supported by more than 100 panels, workshops, fashion-tech runways, networking events and the Washington Elite Investment Summit & Gala across Times Square and New York City from September 10–19, 2026.

Tickets and the complete speaker roster are available at BlockchainWeek.ai.

title: Michael Terpin, Karla Ballard, Lou Kerner Join Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition
excerpt: Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition 2026 announces industry pioneers Michael Terpin, Karla Ballard, and Lou Kerner as new speakers for its landmark Times Square event (Sept 10–19) coinciding with UNGA 81 and New York Fashion Week.
contentHtml:
Three Visionary Leaders Join the Premier Global Gathering

Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition is proud to announce the addition of three influential leaders — Michael Terpin, Karla Ballard, and Lou Kerner — as speakers for its landmark 2026 edition. Taking place September 10–19 in Times Square, New York City, the event coincides with the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA 81) and New York Fashion Week, bringing together global policymakers, innovators, investors, and visionaries at the intersection of blockchain, Bitcoin, AI, energy, space, and real-world impact.

This historic gathering positions blockchain technology at the center of conversations shaping global governance, sustainable development, and technological progress while world leaders from 193 countries convene in New York. The addition of these speakers elevates the program’s depth and reinforces Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition as the premier platform where industry pioneers engage directly with diplomats, institutional decision-makers, and builders.

Michael Terpin

Godfather of Crypto • Founder, Transform Ventures & BitAngels

Widely recognized as the “Godfather of Crypto” by CNBC, Terpin has shaped the blockchain industry for more than a decade. As founder and CEO of Transform Ventures and co-founder of BitAngels — the first multi-city crypto angel network — he played a pivotal role in early ecosystem development. Terpin’s Transform Group pioneered marketing and advisory for landmark projects including Ethereum, Tether, Augur, Bancor, Gnosis, and others. An early Bitcoin investor and author of Bitcoin Supercycle, he developed influential frameworks such as the “Four Seasons of Bitcoin” model and helped establish Puerto Rico as a leading blockchain hub after receiving the first Act 22 tax decree in the sector.

Full Profile

Karla Ballard

Future of Work • Blockchain • Cultural Architect • HUMN

A cultural architect and champion of human-centered blockchain, Ballard is Founder and CEO of HUMN, a platform focused on blockchain infrastructure for communities, skills verification, and the future of work. Ballard’s work emphasizes using distributed ledger technology to record economic contributions, enable peer-to-peer skill-sharing, and build inclusive community economies beyond speculative use cases. A former Independent vice-presidential candidate alongside Brock Pierce in 2020, she has long advocated for blockchain’s potential in transparency, trust, and social impact.

Full Profile

Lou Kerner

Founder, DAIAA + CryptoMondays

Founder of DAIAA and CryptoMondays — the world’s largest crypto-focused Meetup network with chapters across dozens of cities — Kerner has been a dedicated community builder and thought leader since immersing himself full-time in crypto in 2017. Previously called “Wall Street’s Bitcoin Expert” by The Wall Street Journal, Kerner brings experience as a Goldman Sachs equity analyst, early social media executive, and Partner at Blockchain Coinvestors. As a frequent keynote speaker and advocate for real-world adoption and community-first approaches, he has helped scale in-person Web3 networks globally.

Full Profile

STATEMENT FROM ORGANIZERS

“We are especially proud to welcome Michael Terpin, Karla Ballard, and Lou Kerner during this historic meeting of leaders at UNGA 81. Each has made indelible contributions — from pioneering early crypto infrastructure and investment networks, to advancing community-centered blockchain applications for the future of work, to building the largest grassroots crypto communities worldwide. Their presence ensures our discussions on Bitcoin adoption, AI convergence, policy, energy, space, and societal impact will be informed by true visionaries who have already shaped the industries they represent.”

Event Highlights

Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition features a flagship two-day conference on September 16–17 focused on Bitcoin, policy, institutional infrastructure, AI, energy, space, and real-world applications, alongside more than 100 experiences across the full 10-day program. The event uniquely aligns blockchain innovation with the global stage of UNGA, offering unmatched opportunities for dialogue between technologists and the world’s decision-makers.

title: At the Precipice: A Call to Arms for Liberty-Loving People Worldwide
excerpt: We stand at a precipice. For the first time in generations, the world we leave our children looks darker, more constrained, and less free than the one our parents left us. Privacy erodes daily. A powerful call to arms from Bruce Porter Jr. for every liberty-loving person worldwide at Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition 2026.
contentHtml:
By Bruce Porter Jr.

Op-Ed · Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition 2026

We stand at a precipice. For the first time in generations, the world we are preparing to leave our children looks darker, more constrained, and less free than the one our parents left us. Privacy erodes daily. Ownership becomes conditional. Liberty is bargained away for the illusion of temporary safety. And the tools that once promised emancipation now risk becoming instruments of control.

Over the past month I have had the profound honor of speaking with extraordinary individuals—visionaries, builders, freedom fighters, and community leaders—while examining a wealth of speaking proposals for Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition. The conversations have been awe-inspiring. The depth of knowledge and capability gathered in New York City at this critical moment is remarkable. Those discussions, particularly in recent days, compelled me to write this Op-Ed: a clear-eyed assessment and an urgent call to arms for every liberty-loving person on the planet.

In the early days, Bitcoin and blockchain represented something pure and radical. They offered a path to free ourselves from the ever-overreaching hand of bankers whose influence reaches into every branch of government. They promised actual privacy, genuine liberty, and the ability to own something that could not be seized, frozen, discovered, or stopped. Years ago, in an interview, Nick Spanos articulated a truth that has been echoed to me across the globe by liberty leaders, including President Vit: if we do not use blockchain to free ourselves, it will be used to enslave us.

That warning rings louder today. Advances in artificial intelligence accelerate the erosion of freedoms at a pace that feels relentless. Constitutional protections in the United States are violated with alarming regularity, and ordinary people find themselves with little practical means to push back. Privacy is casually sold to the masses under the banner of “the greater good.” We would do well to remember the counsel of our forefathers: those who would give up essential liberty to purchase a little temporary safety deserve neither liberty nor safety.

Yesterday I spoke with a former vice-presidential candidate and the founder of HUMN Blockchain Communities, Karla Ballard. We discussed the torch of liberty and the power of community to create real value for everyone. That conversation was reinforced in person by Lou Kerner, founder of DAIAA and CryptoMondays—someone who has built thriving communities grounded in these same principles. We are humbled and honored that such people will speak at Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition. They are coming to the world’s square to help chart a roadmap for the future we leave our children.

I have said on stages around the world that the blockchain community is, in truth, the strongest community on Earth. We simply have not yet fully recognized it. Across borders, languages, races, and abilities, we share a common belief in liberty, ownership, and privacy. As the great Ron Paul told me during our in-person meeting earlier this year: Liberty is popular. That is why we gather in New York. World leaders, anarchists, bankers, blockheads, and freedom fighters—this event is for all of you. The only viable path forward is together.

Another conversation that left a deep impression was with my old friend Alex Lightman, known for crafting doctrine and best practices for artificial intelligence with the U.S. government, the European Union, and, with a little luck, the United Nations as we convene in New York. Alex has devoted his life to leaving the world better than he found it. He shared his theory and mathematical equation of Survivability. I cannot wait for you to hear him speak.

Additional discussions with Glenn Sorenson and Yoon Auh on privacy and the security of our assets will inject fresh energy and practical solutions into New York City during UNGA 81. These are not abstract debates. They are the conversations and solutions we must have if we intend to reverse the current trajectory.

So I issue this challenge to everyone planning to attend: What is your contribution to the community? How will you help the community, and how will the community help you? And to those still deciding whether to come: make the necessary arrangements. Meet us in New York.

It is time for us to rise.

title: Blockchain Can Help Resolve the Strait of Hormuz Dispute | Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition
excerpt: Iran maintains sovereign rights over the Strait of Hormuz, while the world needs reliable transit. Blockchain technology offers a neutral, transparent framework to manage security, contributions, and international cooperation — moving beyond unilateral tolls and protection money demands.
contentHtml:
Policy Analysis • Maritime Governance • Blockchain

How transparent, rules-based technology can move beyond unilateral tolls and protection money toward verifiable cooperation.

By Guest Contributor • July 13, 2026

The International Maritime Organization (IMO) has stated there is no legal basis for mandatory tolls simply for transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Yet Iran maintains that significant portions of the strait — particularly the northern lanes lying within roughly 10 miles of its shoreline — give it the sovereign right to regulate passage and seek compensation for security and use of its waters.

President Trump has demanded the United States receive the equivalent of 20% of cargo value for providing naval protection. The result has been heightened tensions, ship attacks, U.S. strikes, and rising global oil prices.

This is a clash of competing interpretations: Iran’s assertion of control over waters near its coast versus the international community’s interest in unimpeded transit through a chokepoint that carries roughly 20–25% of global seaborne oil trade.

The Limits of Unilateral Approaches

Unilateral toll demands, selective blockades, and military responses are proving ineffective at delivering long-term stability. Temporary agreements have repeatedly collapsed. Neither Iran’s legitimate security concerns near its coastline nor the global economy’s need for reliable energy flows are being adequately addressed through traditional power politics.

Blockchain as a Neutral, Practical Solution

Blockchain technology offers a practical path forward. A permissioned blockchain platform — coordinated by the IMO or a neutral multi-stakeholder group — could create transparent, verifiable rules that respect both Iran’s geographic position and the need for stable international transit.

Key elements of such a system could include:

  • On-chain verification of routes — Providing Iran with clear, tamper-proof visibility into traffic patterns near its coast.
  • Transparent contribution mechanisms — Usage-based funding for shared security through smart contracts, rather than arbitrary fees.
  • Automated compliance rules — Linking benefits and fund releases to verifiable adherence to agreed traffic schemes.

This approach does not require any party to fully surrender its legal position. Instead, it creates operational trust through immutable and transparent records — something traditional diplomacy has struggled to achieve consistently.

Moving Past the Current Impasse

Neither unilateral territorial claims nor external demands for “protection money” will produce a stable, long-term solution. A blockchain-enabled framework allows stakeholders to operate under clear, auditable rules rather than competing unilateral actions.

The technology to support verifiable, rules-based cooperation already exists. What is needed is the willingness to apply it to one of the world’s most strategically important maritime chokepoints.

About the Author: This article was contributed by a Guest Contributor with expertise at the intersection of maritime security, international relations, and emerging technology.

Disclaimer: The views expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the official policy of any organization.

contentHtml:
PB

Porter Brothers

INSIGHT · INFLUENCE · INTEGRITY

Visit Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT · BLOCKCHAIN WEEK - UNGA EDITION 2026

From Conversation to Commitment “Pause the World for Peace” Joins Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition 2026

The Porter Brothers officially announce that Paul Sladkus’ “Pause the World for Peace” is now an official part of Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition on September 19 in Times Square.

PB

Bruce & David Porter

The Porter Brothers | Founders, Global Boost & Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition

July 2026

6 min read

Last week I had the pleasure of sitting down with Paul Sladkus on his Good News Broadcast. What began as a conversation about blockchain quickly evolved into something much deeper.

We talked about what blockchain really is — a distributed ledger that creates trust without a central authority. We discussed Bitcoin’s fixed supply, the difference between true blockchains and tokens that can be minted endlessly, and why decentralization matters in a world where trust is often in short supply.

Then Paul shared his life’s work: “Pause the World for Peace.” For more than two decades he has championed the International Day of Peace. This year, on the 24th anniversary, he is bringing the movement to Times Square on September 19th — a powerful midday gathering featuring human peace signs, peace messengers, live music, and a collective pause for humanity.

The original interview with Paul Sladkus on Good News Broadcast (July 2026)

OP-ED July 9, 2026 BLOCKCHAIN WEEK - UNGA EDITION PERSPECTIVES

The United Nations General Assembly — where the world meets for peace

Why UNGA 81 Will Be the Most Important General Assembly in History

The United Nations Has Spoken on Iran and Gaza. Now the World Must Answer in New York This September.

By Guest Contributor

PEACE • MULTILATERALISM • ONE HUMAN FAMILY

In recent months the United Nations has issued clear, urgent calls on the escalating violence involving Iran and the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. These statements are not background noise. They are the conscience of the international community speaking directly to every nation on Earth.

The United Nations Has Already Named the Crises

On February 28, 2026, Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the military escalation in the Middle East in the strongest terms, stating that the use of force by the United States and Israel against Iran, and the subsequent retaliation by Iran, “undermine international peace and security.” He called immediately for a cessation of hostilities and de-escalation to prevent a wider regional conflict.

Just weeks ago, as tensions resurfaced with renewed military exchanges between the United States and Iran, the United Nations again spoke through Assistant Secretary-General Elizabeth Spehar at the Security Council. She warned that every new strike increases the risk of miscalculation and welcomed the decision by parties to exercise restraint and de-escalate.

At the same time, United Nations humanitarian agencies have continued to sound the alarm on the dire situation in Gaza and the occupied Palestinian territory — restrictions on aid, ongoing violence, and the desperate need for safe, unhindered humanitarian access.

The United Nations has not remained silent. Through its Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, it has determined that the actions in Gaza constitute genocide. At the same time, the Secretary-General and UN agencies continue to urge immediate de-escalation, protection of civilians, and full humanitarian access.

“These are not abstract conflicts. They are human tragedies unfolding in real time. The United Nations exists precisely for moments like these.”

UNGA 81: The Moment History Is Watching

This September, the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly convenes in New York City. World leaders, foreign ministers, and heads of state will gather under one roof — the only truly universal forum where every nation, large and small, has an equal voice.

Never in recent memory has the need for collective action been more urgent. The crises in the Middle East have shown that unilateral actions and bilateral deals alone cannot deliver lasting peace. Only through the multilateral framework of the United Nations can nations come together to negotiate, compromise, and build sustainable solutions that protect civilians and prevent wider war.

United Nations General Assembly Hall, New York

The Moral Authority to Lead

The United Nations carries unique moral authority because it represents all of humanity. Its Charter, signed by 193 member states, remains the highest expression of our shared commitment to peace, human dignity, and international cooperation. When the Secretary-General and UN officials speak, they speak not for one nation or one bloc — they speak for the collective conscience of the world.

Behind every UN statement stand the voices of countless diplomats, humanitarian workers, and the peoples of every continent who believe that dialogue is stronger than division and that peace is possible when we choose it together.

A Call to Every Leader on Earth

This September, the table is set in New York City. The United Nations General Assembly and Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition will bring together heads of state, policymakers, technologists, civil society, and citizens from every corner of the globe.

I call on every leader — from the largest powers to the smallest nations — to come to New York not merely to speak, but to listen, to negotiate in good faith, and to commit to concrete steps toward peace. The people of the world are watching. Our children are watching.

“We are one human species. The crises we face today do not respect borders. Neither should our solutions.”

Let us use this historic gathering to chart a path forward together — one that ends cycles of violence, restores hope to suffering populations, and builds lasting peace through dialogue and cooperation. The United Nations gives us the forum. The moment gives us the urgency. The only question is whether we will seize it.

Come to New York this September. Stand with the United Nations. Choose peace — together.

One human species. One shared future. One United Nations.

A fractured world meets the promise of decentralized technology

IN A FRACTURED WORLD

By Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition Team

MULTILATERALISM • BLOCKCHAIN • HUMANITARIAN IMPACT

The headlines coming out of the United Nations this week are sobering. Two powerful earthquakes have devastated parts of Venezuela, killing at least 235 people and leaving millions in urgent need. In the Strait of Hormuz, the UN’s International Maritime Organization was forced to suspend a major seafarer evacuation after an attack on a commercial vessel. And the Security Council has issued grave warnings that El Obeid in Sudan risks becoming the site of new mass atrocities.

The United Nations: Still Our Best Hope

The United Nations was founded to prevent exactly this kind of fragmentation. It remains the only institution where nearly every nation has a voice. Yet the scale and speed of today’s challenges are testing its traditional tools. Centralized aid systems move too slowly. Transparency is often lacking. And too many people affected by crises remain powerless.

Blockchain: A Decentralized Force for Real Progress

This is where the global blockchain community has a critical role to play. Over the past decade, decentralized technology has already delivered the most significant shift in monetary systems in generations. It proved that coordination, trust, and ownership can exist without centralized gatekeepers.

Recent UN-coordinated responses to crises like the Venezuela earthquakes

From verifiable humanitarian aid tracking to secure coordination tools in conflict zones, blockchain offers practical solutions that can make multilateral efforts more effective.

Why Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition During UNGA 81 Matters More Than Ever

This September, during UNGA 81, the world’s leaders will gather in New York. At the same time, the blockchain community has reached a level of maturity where it can deliver real-world impact. That convergence is why Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition will be the most important event we have organized in four years.

The meeting of global institutions and decentralized technology

This is not just another conference. It is a deliberate meeting point between the world’s most important multilateral institution and the most dynamic decentralized ecosystem.

“The blockchain community has already changed money. The next chapter must be changing how we deliver peace, protect human dignity, and safeguard liberty for future generations.”

A Call for Freedom, Privacy, and Ownership

We must continue pushing for freedom, privacy, and ownership — not just in finance, but across all systems that affect people’s lives. Our children and future generations deserve to inherit a world where technology serves liberty rather than control.

The world does not have to keep choosing between death and destruction. It can choose to build.

IN A FRACTURED WORLD

By Guest Contributor

MULTILATERALISM • BLOCKCHAIN • PEACE

World leaders convening at UNGA 81 in New York City

As the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA 81) prepares to convene in New York City this September, the world’s attention turns once again to the iconic headquarters on the East River. From September 8 to 22, 2026—with the high-level General Debate kicking off on September 22—delegations from all 193 member states will gather. Over 150 heads of state and government are expected to attend in person, delivering national statements and engaging in bilateral diplomacy on the most pressing issues of our time.

A World Defined by Deepening Fractures

This is no ordinary diplomatic gathering. The global landscape in mid-2026 is defined by deepening fractures: protracted conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East continue to exact a devastating human and economic toll, with risks of spillover and hybrid warfare threatening broader stability. Geoeconomic confrontation looms large, as trade restrictions, energy disruptions, and supply-chain vulnerabilities compound inflation and the threat of downturn. When multilateral talks risk deadlock, blockchain provides immutable records that all parties can verify independently. When peace feels elusive, technologies that reduce information asymmetry and rent-seeking create conditions for durable cooperation.

For anyone—diplomat, entrepreneur, activist, or citizen—committed to peace and collaborative problem-solving, Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition is not optional. It is essential. It is where the conversations that will shape the next decade of global governance actually happen: pragmatic, forward-looking, and rooted in technologies that transcend borders and bureaucracies. As world leaders deliver their addresses at UNGA 81, the real work of building a more stable, equitable, and peaceful century may well be forged in the parallel sessions, networking rooms, and demo stages just blocks away.

The choice before us is clear. We can continue relying solely on 20th-century institutions to manage 21st-century crises, or we can harness the tools of decentralization to complement and strengthen multilateralism. Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition 2026 invites us to choose the latter—with urgency, creativity, and shared purpose.

The world cannot afford to wait. See you in New York this September.

OP-ED MAY 16, 2026 BLOCKCHAIN WEEK - UNGA EDITION PERSPECTIVES

Featured: The United Nations meets blockchain in the neon future

Lessons from the Trump-Xi Summit and the Ever-More-Powerful Banking Cartel

By Guest Contributor

MULTILATERALISM • BLOCKCHAIN • SOVEREIGNTY

Trump and Xi Jinping at the Beijing Summit 2026

Just days ago, President Trump concluded a high-profile bilateral summit with Xi Jinping in Beijing. While the two leaders celebrated new trade agreements, the meeting once again highlighted a dangerous trend: superpowers increasingly prefer private bilateral deals over the multilateral institutions designed to protect the global majority.

International Law Is Being Ignored — Bilateral Deals Are the New Normal

From protracted conflicts that defy UN resolutions to unilateral sanctions and backroom superpower summits, the post-1945 rules-based order is under unprecedented strain. The recent Trump-Xi talks — focused on tariffs, technology, and geopolitics — are the latest example of major powers writing their own rules while the United Nations Security Council and General Assembly are sidelined.

Yet the United Nations remains the only truly global forum where 193 member states — from the smallest island nations to the largest economies — can debate, negotiate, and forge consensus. Dismissing the UN because it is imperfect is to surrender the last meaningful arena capable of restraining raw power politics.

United Nations General Assembly Hall, New York

The Banking Cartel’s Growing Shadow

While geopolitics fractures into bilateral deals, a different kind of power consolidates: the ever-more-powerful banking cartel. Central banks, major commercial institutions, the IMF, and the World Bank continue to shape a global financial system in which debt, monetary policy, and access to capital determine the fate of entire nations.

Developing countries remain trapped in cycles of structural adjustment and crushing interest payments that dwarf their ability to invest in health, education, or climate resilience. Meanwhile, financial elites enjoy bailouts and policy influence that ordinary citizens can scarcely comprehend.

“The banking cartel thrives on opacity and central control. Blockchain offers radical transparency and individual sovereignty. The UN offers the global stage. Together they can restore balance.”

Decentralized blockchain technology as a force for transparency

Blockchain as the People’s Counterweight

This is where the technologies at the heart of Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition become revolutionary. Decentralized ledgers, Bitcoin, smart contracts, and transparent on-chain governance are not anti-UN — they are powerful force multipliers for the very multilateral ideals the UN was founded to uphold.

Imagine UN aid programs audited in real time on public blockchains, tokenized development finance that bypasses extractive intermediaries, and decentralized identity systems that give the unbanked real economic standing — without asking permission from any cartel.

The future: Multilateral governance meets decentralized technology

A Call to Action at Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition 2026

As we gather in New York this September during the United Nations General Assembly and New York Fashion Week, let us move beyond panels and handshakes. Blockchain builders, policymakers, and civil society leaders must commit to concrete partnerships that strengthen multilateral institutions while equipping ordinary people with the financial tools they need to resist concentrated power.

The era of ignoring international law while a banking cartel writes the rules is unsustainable. The United Nations gives us the forum. Blockchain gives us the technology. The only missing ingredient is collective will.

People must get together. The table is already set — it is called the United Nations.
